info.title: Perfox Platform API
info.description: Server-to-server API for external agents and integrations. Authenticate with a tenant API key: `Authorization: Bearer sk_…`. Every operation is scoped to the key's tenant.

prompt.description: Plain-language description of the agent to build.

post.description: Create-or-find a customer by phone/email/external_id (E.164 normalized, deduped) and apply identity fields. Idempotent on identity.

get.summary: A customer's details — quick stats and insights

channels.description: Every channel the customer has used, busiest first.

channel_mix.description: Conversations touching each channel; one that moved channel counts once per channel.

ended.description: Closed by the system without a resolved verdict (e.g. idle timeout, call ended).

get.description: Identity, quick stats (total conversations, channels used, customer since, last active) and insights (channel mix, resolution rate) for one customer, computed over ALL their conversations. Resolution rate uses the same definition as /analytics/summary. The conversations themselves: GET /customers/{id}/conversations.

Every conversation this customer has had, newest first. Optional `status` filter. Pages with an opaque `next_cursor`, so conversations started while you page are never skipped. Read a transcript with GET /conversations/{id}/events.

post.summary: Link an identifier combination to your external_id
post.description: Register a business identity link: map an identifier combination (email/mobile[+name]) to YOUR external_id. Combinations are AND — {email, name} separates family members sharing an email. APPLIED NOW: an existing customer consistent with EVERY identifier you send (sharing one of them is not enough) gets the external_id immediately (`applied_customer_id` in the response); otherwise it applies at that person's first contact, on every channel. Customers are NEVER merged: identifiers that match two existing customers, or a customer already linked to another id, are refused with 409 `identity_conflict`. Linking identifiers that an existing link to a DIFFERENT external_id would also match is refused with 409 `link_conflict` — DELETE the old link first. Re-sending the identical link is idempotent.

external_id.description: Your system's stable user id this combination maps to.

mobile.description: Any format; canonicalized to E.164 server-side.

name.description: Discriminator for shared email/mobile (e.g. family members).

get.summary: Read back the links to your external_id

schema.description: Your system's id — every link to it is read / removed.

get.description: Every identifier combination currently linked to this external_id, and which existing customer each was applied to — use it to confirm a link took effect.

delete.summary: Remove the links to your external_id

schema.description: Your system's id — every link to it is read / removed.

delete.description: Removes every link to this external_id (undo an import, remove a person) and undoes what these link calls applied: the external_id is cleared from each customer listed as `applied_customer_id`, only if that customer still carries this same id. A customer that got the id any other way (created under it at first contact, widget identify, your lookup_customer tool) keeps it and keeps resolving to it. For a data-subject erasure use the DPDP erasure request, which also removes that person's links.

post.summary: Link up to 500 identifier combinations in one call
post.description: The batch form of POST /customer/link for bulk imports: up to 500 links, each applied and reported on its own (`linked`, `link_conflict` or `identity_conflict`). One item's conflict never stops the others.

external_id.description: Your system's stable user id this combination maps to.

mobile.description: Any format; canonicalized to E.164 server-side.

name.description: Discriminator for shared email/mobile (e.g. family members).

get.summary: List cases (the case-management view of conversations)

schema.description: Return events created strictly AFTER this ISO timestamp — pass the `next_after` from the previous page.
Return events created strictly BEFORE this ISO timestamp.

Comma-separated opt-in payloads: `tool_io` (tool_input/tool_output on tool events), `files` (attachment metadata + a short-lived signed file_url on file_upload events), `structured` (a structured reply — WhatsApp buttons/list/template/media envelope — as readable `text` plus the typed `message` object, instead of raw JSON), `delivery` (`status`/`message_id`/`error` on delivery_status events; `origin`/`message_id`/`outbound_message_id` on a platform send). Omitted by default so existing consumers see an unchanged response. (A template or media send made with POST /messages used to carry no `text`; it now carries its label, e.g. `[template: <name>]`, in the default projection too.)

tool_status.description: TRANSPORT outcome of the call (success | error | timeout) — NOT the business result. A tool that returned `{success:false}` is still `success` here; read tool_output.

file_url.description: Short-lived signed download URL, minted on read. Never the durable storage key.

message.description: The structured reply as sent (the WhatsApp envelope: `type` + its fields). `text` then carries its readable label.

message_id.description: The provider message id — the same id the `message.status` webhook carries.

error.description: delivery_status events: the provider failure reason, when failed.

origin.description: Set on a platform-initiated send (`public_api_outbound` for POST /messages or POST /outbound).

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page.

get.description: Returns the conversation_events transcript. By DEFAULT a safe subset (text + tool name/status); debug payloads and PII hashes are always excluded. Pass `include=tool_io` for tool_input/tool_output, `include=files` for attachment metadata plus a short-lived signed file_url, `include=structured` for readable structured replies plus the typed `message`, `include=delivery` for delivery status and send ids. Paginate with `limit` + `after` (use the returned `next_after`); filter with `event_type`.

post.description: Register a tenant MCP tool server (the agents call OUT to it). Tools are live-discovered. The auth credential is stored but NEVER returned (only `has_credential`).

patch.description: Edit a connected MCP tool server IN PLACE — url, transport, auth type/header/secret, or limits. The server id and its stored credential id are preserved, so rotating a key never orphans the agents that use its tools. Omit or blank `auth_secret` to keep the current secret (it is never returned by any read). Tools are re-discovered only when the url or the auth actually changed.

post.description: File a ticket with the Skillmine support teams from your own tooling. `category` routes it: `forward_deployment` for help with your implementation, `platform` for a suspected platform defect. Optionally attribute it to one of your workspace users with `requester_email`; omit to raise it as the API integration. Attachments are not supported on this surface yet — reference a link in the description.

get.description: Every ticket raised by your workspace, newest activity first, however it was raised (Studio, API or the support chatbot).
One ticket with its full message thread.

post.description: Add a message to a ticket you raised. Replying to a resolved or awaiting-customer ticket re-opens it.

get.description: Total conversations, resolution rate, token usage and channel mix for a window, in one call. Use `days` for a rolling window, or explicit `start_date`/`end_date`.
Voice conversations (phone + web voice), newest first, with duration and recording availability. Cursor-paged: pass the returned `next_cursor` back as `cursor`.
Short-lived signed URLs for the caller, AI and combined stereo legs. Links expire — fetch them when the player opens, do not store them.
Token totals plus a per-bucket series for the window.

post.description: Start an outbound conversation on phone, sms, whatsapp or email using a PUBLISHED agent that has a Trigger node for that channel. A phone call always opens a NEW conversation (a call is a session, not a thread); text channels continue the open thread. Check `send_authorized` in the response: on email/sms/whatsapp the agent can only send if the matching Sender node is wired on its canvas. A text message that was sent returns `message_id` (ours, always present) and `provider_message_id` (the carrier's, may be empty); it goes out from the number on the agent's inbound Trigger, so replies return to the same agent.

Send a message YOU compose, on WhatsApp. `channel` is optional but must be `whatsapp` if sent — any other value is REFUSED rather than silently delivered on WhatsApp; for sms/email/phone use POST /outbound. Exactly one of: `text` (free text), `media` (an image, audio clip, video or document by PUBLIC URL), `location` (a map pin), or `template` (an approved template). Inside WhatsApp's 24-hour service window any of them is deliverable; OUTSIDE it only a template is. Identify the sender with `from` (your business number, which resolves the agent that owns it) or with `agent_id` directly; exactly one. No AI runs — what you pass is what is sent. 🛑 MEDIA IS FETCHED BY THE PROVIDER from the URL you give, so it must be publicly reachable and stay reachable until it has been fetched; a link that expires in seconds is the usual cause of a media message that "sent" and never arrived. Audio takes no caption (Meta has no field for it) and `filename` applies to documents only — both are refused rather than silently dropped. 🛑 An owning agent with no WhatsApp Sender action on its canvas is refused with 422 `sender_not_authorized` BEFORE anything is written, so nothing is ever recorded as sent when nothing went out. Use the returned `id` with GET /messages/{id} to follow delivery.

get.description: Messages you sent, newest first. Filter by `to`, `from`, `status`, and a `since`/`until` window. Pages with an opaque `next_cursor` rather than an offset, so rows written while you page are never skipped.

The current delivery state of a message you sent, plus its transition history. `sent` means the provider ACCEPTED it; `delivered` and `read` arrive asynchronously from the carrier, and `failed` carries the provider's reason.

post.summary: Pull the latest templates from your WhatsApp providers
post.description: Ask every connected WhatsApp provider for its templates and record what came back, so `GET /api/v1/templates` can answer without touching a provider. THIS is where the provider cost lives: Meta returns everything in one call, but Plivo's list is a summary projection, so each template needs its own read — and Plivo rate-limits those (measured: 11 templates drew HTTP 429 on three). Sync retries a 429 with backoff; a read cannot, which is why the two are separate. Returns how many rows were recorded, how many CHANGED since last time, and how many the providers have stopped reporting (marked absent, never deleted). 🛑 `errors` is part of a SUCCESSFUL sync: a connection that could not be asked — a Plivo credential with no WABA id, an expired Meta token — is named while the providers that answered are still recorded.

get.summary: List the stored WhatsApp templates and what each one needs filled in
get.description: Every template across your WhatsApp connections WITH ITS STATUS, and WHAT TO FILL IN for each one. The list is NOT filtered — `pending`, `rejected`, `paused`, `disabled` and `unknown` rows come back too, because "why can I not send this one" is a question the status answers; only `approved` is sendable and checking it is yours to do. Outside WhatsApp's 24-hour service window a template is the only thing deliverable, and `POST /api/v1/messages` takes one by `name` — this is how you discover which names exist and what they need. Each row carries `params`: `body_parameter_count` (how many ordered values `template.body_parameters` must carry), the approved `body_text` so you can see what you are filling, a `header` when the approved header takes a per-send value, and the `buttons` needing one — each with its index in the APPROVED button list, because Meta fills buttons by index. 🛑 `params` ABSENT means the provider row carried no readable components, i.e. UNDETERMINED — not "nothing to fill"; sending no values then fails after acceptance as a delivery-receipt 350. Only `status: "approved"` is sendable. Served from the copy this workspace holds, so it never touches a provider and never inherits their rate limits — `synced_at` says when that copy was last refreshed by `POST /api/v1/templates/sync`. 🛑 `synced_at: null` means this workspace has NEVER synced, which is a different statement from "you have no approved templates": an empty list WITH a timestamp means the providers genuinely reported none. Approval is asynchronous and the provider owns `status`, so a stored verdict can lag — sync before acting on one if it matters. The fill spec does not lag: body text, placeholder count, header and buttons are fixed when a template is approved.

post.summary: Subscribe to inbound messages and delivery events
post.description: Register an HTTPS endpoint to receive `message.inbound` (a customer wrote to you) and `message.status` (a message you sent changed delivery state). 🛑 The signing `secret` is returned ONCE, here — it is stored encrypted and never shown again. Every delivery carries `X-Perfox-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256>` over `<t>.<raw body>`; verify it against the RAW body before parsing. Deliveries retry with exponential backoff and carry a stable `X-Perfox-Delivery` id you can use for idempotency.

get.description: Your endpoints, with their health: consecutive failures, the last delivery, and the last error verbatim. A subscription the platform disabled after repeated failures carries `disabled_reason`.

patch.description: Change the URL or events, or set `status` back to `active` after the platform disabled it. Re-enabling clears the failure counter, so a fixed endpoint is not disabled again by its own history. 🛑 Send `rotate_secret: true` to mint a NEW signing secret — returned once, in this response, exactly as at creation. The old secret stops signing immediately, so a leaked one can be retired without deleting the subscription and going deaf in between; this is the only way back from a lost secret, because there is no route that reads one.

post.description: POST a signed synthetic event to the endpoint and report what it answered — SYNCHRONOUSLY, so you can debug your signature check without waiting for real traffic. The event is `webhook.test`, which cannot be subscribed to and is never emitted by the platform, so a test can never be mistaken for a real message. It does not retry, does not count toward failures, and cannot disable the subscription.
